title: Alibaba's New AI Chip (Zhenwu V900) & China Data-Center Buildout
summary: Gotrade News - Alibaba unveiled its most advanced in-house artificial-intelligence processor, the Zhenwu V900, and set a target of more than 20 gigawatts
body_markdown:
## SMIC Manufacturing and the US Export-Control Backdrop


According to[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/alibabas-zhenwu-v900-chip-and-what-it-means-for-chinas-foundry-ecosystem-93CH-4909867) , the V900 is produced by Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), and Alibaba describes the part as domestically manufactured, a framing driven by US export restrictions that cut Chinese AI-chip designers off from foreign foundries.


The same report frames the shift as a structural win for SMIC and a structural headwind for[Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/tsm/) , which stands to forgo Chinese AI-chip manufacturing volume as production moves onshore.


For investors, the read-through is a Chinese semiconductor supply chain being rebuilt vertically and at speed. That same export-control dynamic has shaped cross-border tech sentiment, a theme running through recent[US-China summit optimism that lifted Asian and global equities](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/us-china-summit-optimism-lifts-asian-global-equities/) .


## 20 GW Data-Center Target by 2032 and the Nvidia Question


The 20-gigawatt capacity goal, reported by[Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4645223-alibaba-steps-up-ai-push-with-v900-chip-20-gw-data-center-target) , is the demand side of the strategy, signaling that Alibaba intends to consume large volumes of its own silicon inside its cloud.


The competitive question sits with[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) , whose accelerators remain the global benchmark. A credible domestic alternative can narrow Nvidia's addressable share inside China even as demand elsewhere stays firm, though neither fetched report offered a direct performance benchmark between the V900 and Nvidia's current parts.


Investors using[Gotrade](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/) can track the US-listed names most exposed to this shift, from the incumbent chip leaders to the foundry supply chain, as the story develops toward the V900's 2027 production ramp.
